extra_quotes: We measure the MOT temperature using time-of-flight (TOF) absorption imaging 45,46.
We measure the MOT atom number using two independent methods: absorption imaging and fluorescence detection 47,48.

The absolute frequency stability of the SAS-locked cooling laser is measured against a self-referenced fiber frequency comb (Vescent FFC-100) whose repetition rate is phase-locked to a 1 Hz-linewidth ULE-cavity-stabilized laser (Stable Laser Systems) / Rb-disciplined, GPS-referenced oscillator (SRS-FS725).

The limitations of the present implementation arise from the actuators rather than the photonic architecture. The ring intensity modulator provides 6.3 dB of extinction, but only 2.2 dB can presently be used because tuning its resonance close to the laser frequency introduces resonant back-reflection that injection-locks the cooling laser and pulls it from the SAS lock point (Extended Data Fig. 5).

The thermo-optic actuators also limit the intensity-control bandwidth to approximately 2 kHz, so full extinction during time-of-flight measurements currently requires switching off the cooling-laser current.
